questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Personal connection, language of teaching, studying in somewhere outside of europe

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: easy as UBA provided a whole guide about housing,  getting from the airport to the city, etc.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: guide beforehands and and orientation meeting, plus the possibility to always speak to the coordinators

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was very helpful but the system was sometimes  more complicated

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: easy, recommend pages like zonaprop or argenprop

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I think you cannot really live on campus

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was kind of long  but felt easy as they explained it in the meeting, send aus a powerpoint with clear instructions and were available for any questions

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to register in person, but beforehand you get two weeks to try out different courses which is kind of nice

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: coordinators and international office. Most of the professors were also very opened and happy to help with anything

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: very successful as you coul swap them in the first weeks

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: do not stress. It can seem overwhelming but there is always someone to help you

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was limited to the choices because I was an MA stundents doing BA courses so I had to do advanced once, but overall there were good choices available

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Did BA courses as the contract between the unis is only for BA, but given that the BA in Argentina lasts  in between 4-6 years, the more advanced courses are definitely suitable for Master students

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: similar, depending on  if it was a lecture is was more theoretical and otherwise more practical

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Estado y Derechos Humanos en LATAM 
Migraciones y derechos Humanos- abordaje desde el trabajo social 
Derechos Humanos en un mundo en transición: Cuidados, crisis climatica y movilidad humana 
La sociología de los estudios poscoloniales

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Honestly all, but specifically the latter two as the  professors were super encouraging and helpful! It was a good mix of theory, discussion,  practical stuff even including field trips and guest lectures

Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: a big variety of sports and in my faculty specially political associations

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sports! I did female Futsal and it was a great way to emet local students and also alumni

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: daytrips, explore the city, travel but don't forget to experience life in Buenos Aires as it is great

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: easy but I am Half Argentinian so I might  the wrong person to answer this

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: do sports and speak to people as everyone is very opened and interested

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none, but again I might be the wrong person here

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: flexibility of the people

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: change money at western union, as is is the best exchange rate specially during inflation! Don't stress something might work "worse" in Argentina but there is always a solution to everything an dpeople are willing to help. Enjoy!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: getting used to the exam system

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no

questions.answer: Yes
